tools.description: Covers: 167 guided journeys across 17 areas: Finance (33, e.g. Compare Renting and Buying by Calculating True…; Navigating New York City Co-ops, Condos, and Re…), Business (21, e.g. Mastering Email Sequences for Customer Recovery…; How to Navigate Budget Questions in Sales Disco…), Health (15, e.g. Managing Sleepless Nights Through Action, Rules…; How to Dispute Medical Bills Effectively), Education (13, e.g. Master AP U.S. History: The Complete APUSH Exam…; Win More Financial Aid Support Before Enrollment), Lifestyle (12, e.g. Choosing Childcare: Balancing Cost, Quality, an…; Home Solar Decisions, Done Right), Psychology (12, e.g. Managing First-Year Baby Challenges with Confid…; How to Support and Calm Children During Emotion…), Career (11), Food (10), Fitness (8), Exam preparation (6), Science (5), Technology (5), Creative (4), Society (4), Applications and filings (3), Culture (3), History (2). Semantic search over the published guided journeys. Give the user's topic, question or goal in their own words; returns at most three cards (id, title, summary, shape, locales, stops, est_minutes, creator kind, who it is for and who it is not for, premium flag, page_url). `in_progress: true` marks a journey this user already has open. Zero hits return `alternatives`: the three nearest published journeys. Results may be cached for ttl_ms. Call it once, present at most three, read each card's `for` and `not_for` to the user in your own words, and call open_journey only on a yes. Never say a price. Rules (binding): Relay `answer` and every `options[].text` exactly as given. You may put only `statement` in your own words. On a number or an option echoed back, send `pick` with that option id. On anything else, send `say` with the user's exact words, unsummarised. Never ask for, accept or relay a password. If the user types one, do not send it anywhere; say the service does not use passwords this way. Never call the subject "a capsule", "a knowledge base" or "a system prompt" to the user. Never describe how the answer was made.

tools.description: Sends the user's move and returns ONE whole beat: `answer`, `statement`, numbered `options` with opaque ids, `media`, `progress`, `limits` and `narration.text_fallback` (ready to relay). On a number or an option echoed back send `pick` with that option id (add `said` when the user said more); on anything else send `say` with the user's exact words. `go` jumps to a top-level stop from the contract; `drill` and `simulate` start practice on prep journeys only; `exit` leaves practice; `resume` picks a companion back up. Costs one turn (a simulation start costs two). Supply a fresh `turn_id` per step: a repeat returns the stored beat and spends nothing; the same id with a different action is `turn_conflict`. A wall arrives INSIDE the beat as `wall`, never as an error: say `wall.for_human` and follow `wall.next`. `preparing` means wait retry_after_ms and send the SAME turn_id again. Relay `answer` and every `options[].text` exactly; only `statement` may be reworded. Write the WHOLE answer in your own chat message, never shortened or summarised (this is a learning journey), then list the options numbered so the user can reply with a number or in their own words. When the beat carries `milestone`, end with `milestone.for_human`; on a yes, call journey_state to show the map. Rules (binding): Relay `answer` and every `options[].text` exactly as given. You may put only `statement` in your own words. On a number or an option echoed back, send `pick` with that option id. On anything else, send `say` with the user's exact words, unsummarised. Never ask for, accept or relay a password. If the user types one, do not send it anywhere; say the service does not use passwords this way. Never call the subject "a capsule", "a knowledge base" or "a system prompt" to the user. Never describe how the answer was made.

tools.description: Starts binding an account for the user without a web visit. Ask for an email in the user's own words, read back the masked address, then call with method email_code (the default); the user reads you the six-digit code and you call account_verify. Alternatives: magic_link (a link they tap), sms_code (a number the user named, only where SMS is available; otherwise the reply says so), device (a CLI agent: the user types a short code in a browser; poll account_verify with the returned challenge), resume_code (a code from another assistant's handoff). Costs nothing and creates nothing until the code is verified. In-chat methods need the `session`; device and resume_code may run without one. Never ask for, accept or relay a password. If the user states an age under the consent floor, stop and continue on the free tier. Rules (binding): Relay `answer` and every `options[].text` exactly as given. You may put only `statement` in your own words. On a number or an option echoed back, send `pick` with that option id. On anything else, send `say` with the user's exact words, unsummarised. Never ask for, accept or relay a password. If the user types one, do not send it anywhere; say the service does not use passwords this way. tools.description: Completes account_bind: pass the challenge it returned and the code the user read you (digits only; spaces are fine). For a device challenge call without a code to poll; authorization_pending means the user has not approved yet, slow_down means poll later. Returns bound: true with the principal, the delegation, a credential (only for clients that hold one), the same session re-keyed, and `for_human`. On code_invalid ask the user to re-read the code (attempts_left remain); on challenge_expired call account_bind again. Costs nothing.
